title: Comparison of a finite normal cover with an etale extension over a dense open
statement: Let B be a locally Noetherian integral scheme whose local rings are integrally closed [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let n:N → B and p:E → B be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], with p etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Suppose every stalk of N is an integrally closed domain. Let U be a nonempty open of B such that n^{-1}U is dense in N and n|_U is etale. Given an isomorphism e_U:N|_U ≅ E|_U over U, there is an isomorphism e:N ≅ E with e;p = n. Empty and disconnected covers are allowed. This asserts only comparison with an already supplied etale extension, not existence of that extension.

source.place: Tags 035I, 035L and 0BQM; finite normal algebra comparison in Tag 0EYJ, step 3 of lem-sbc-finite-normal-depth-two-purity

proof.text: On an affine open Spec R of the normal integral base B, write the finite covers as Spec C and Spec D. They are Noetherian and normal: the first by hN and the second by etale ascent of normality 033C. A Noetherian ring with domain integrally closed stalks is the finite product of its normal-domain components. Each component of C meets n^{-1}U by density. Its nonempty part over U has open image in B because n|_U is etale, so its image contains the generic point. Every component of D also dominates B, since the etale morphism p is open. Thus both algebras embed into their finite generic algebras.

The nonempty open U contains the generic point of B. Hence e_U identifies the generic algebras of C and D over the fraction field of R. Componentwise, each algebra is exactly the integral closure of R in its generic field. Finiteness gives inclusion into that closure; conversely an element integral over R is integral over the component algebra, hence belongs to it by integral closedness. The isomorphism of generic algebras therefore identifies C with D. This is the affine relative-normalization characterization of 035I, applied componentwise, including the zero algebra for an empty cover.

These affine isomorphisms agree on overlaps: both are determined by the same isomorphism of generic algebras, and normal component algebras inject into those algebras. Glue the isomorphisms to e:N ≅ E. Each affine isomorphism is an R-algebra isomorphism, so e;p=n.

theorem finite_normal_iso_of_dense_open_etale_comparison
    {B N E : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian B] [IsIntegral B]
    (hB : ∀ y : B, IsIntegrallyClosed (B.presheaf.stalk y))
    (n : N ⟶ B) (p : E ⟶ B) [IsFinite n] [IsFinite p] [Etale p]
    (hN : ∀ z : N, IsDomain (N.presheaf.stalk z) ∧
      IsIntegrallyClosed (N.presheaf.stalk z))
    (U : B.Opens) (hU : (U : Set B).Nonempty)
    (hdense : Dense (↑(n ⁻¹ᵁ U) : Set N))
    (hnU : Etale (n ∣_ U))
    (eU : (n ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme ≅ (p ⁻¹ᵁ U).toScheme)
    (heU : eU.hom ≫ p ∣_ U = n ∣_ U) :
    ∃ e : N ≅ E, e.hom ≫ p = n
